c.tagline: Desert gateway to the Kaluts, built around a magnificent Safavid bazaar.

taxi.fareNote: Foreign credit/debit cards do NOT work anywhere in Iran due to sanctions — bring enough cash (US dollars or euros) to exchange into rial, or arrange a local tourist debit card. Pay taxis in cash; app rides (Snapp/Tapsi) settle in cash too unless you have an Iranian bank card.

emergency.note: 110 is police, 115 is emergency medical/ambulance, and 125 reaches the fire brigade.

solo.f: comfortable; hijab and modest dress required

avoid.reason: No no-go areas in the city itself, but avoid overland routes toward the Sistan-Baluchestan border region to the southeast.

hood_desc: The historic heart of Kerman, wrapped around the Safavid-era Ganjali Khan complex — its square, mosque, bathhouse and caravanserai — and the sprawling covered Grand Bazaar with its spice arcades, teahouses and the Jameh Mosque; best for first-time visitors who want the sights on their doorstep.

The city's central hub around Azadi (Freedom) Square, a busy roundabout where the main boulevards meet, lined with banks, shops, snack stands and taxi stops; a convenient, well-connected base for getting anywhere in town.

A modern tree-lined boulevard that is Kerman's main dining and going-out strip, packed with restaurants, fast-food joints, cafes and hotels; the liveliest street in this conservative city once the sun goes down.
The leafy campus district in the southeast around Shahid Bahonar University, a calm, student-flavoured area of dorms, bookshops and cheap eateries set against the mountains; quiet and local.
A long commercial artery running off the old centre, densely packed with shops, textile and carpet dealers, gold sellers and everyday markets; the place to shop and watch daily Kermani life.

water.note: Tap is treated but bottled water is safer here.

transit.hours: Buses generally run from around 6:00 AM to about 9–10:00 PM; after that, ride-hailing apps (Snapp/Tapsi) or shared taxis fill the gap.
transit.note: Alcohol is banned nationwide, so evening life centres on teahouses and dining rather than bars. Buses and shared taxis are cheap but signage is in Persian; Snapp and Tapsi apps make getting around far easier for visitors.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the driver or with a rechargeable local bus card tapped on board; single rides are very cheap. There is no metro, and foreign bank cards cannot be used, so carry small rial notes.

air: Kerman Airport (Ayatollah Hashemi Rafsanjani Airport, KER)
bus: Adineh Bus Terminal — intercity coaches to Yazd, Shiraz, Bandar Abbas, Isfahan and Tehran
train: Kerman Railway Station — Trans-Iranian line with services to Tehran, Yazd and Bandar Abbas, plus connections toward Bam and Zahedan

airport.name: Kerman Airport (Ayatollah Hashemi Rafsanjani Airport, KER)

transit.m: Airport taxi to the city centre (~15 min)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up a taxi fare or restaurant bill is a kind gesture but tipping is not part of the culture.
